messages.author: e53f91d0708becab
messages.subject: Cut wave
parts:
When analysing animal sound records, one will usually try to retain
(e.g. with specprop() ) some parameters from calls.
In order to analyse individual 'calls' , how can we 'auto-cut a wave
file, isolating individual 'calls' to get parameters for each one? Is
this feasible?

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Cut wave
parts:
Le 31/05/2011 23:43, Paulo E. Cardoso a écrit : 
When analysing animal sound records, one will usually try to retain
(e.g. with specprop() ) some parameters from calls.
In order to analyse individual 'calls' , how can we 'auto-cut a wave
file, isolating individual 'calls' to get parameters for each one? Is
this feasible?

Dear Paulo,

Yes it is feasible with seewave 1.6.0 but this will be much easier and faster with the next version 1.6.1. You can get 1.6.1 here but I do not guarantee that this version is fully stable. It is still in devlopment and did not run the checks.

Anyway, here is the code for the first 'note' of the song 'tico'. You just need to write a loop to achieve the same for all 'notes' or 'calls' of the song you want to analyse

library(seewave)
data(tico)
pos <- timer(tico, f=22050, threshold=5, msmooth=c(50,0), plot=FALSE)
start <- pos$s.start
end <- pos$s.end
note1 <- cutw(tico, from=start[1], to=end[1], out="Wave")
spec <- meanspec(note1, plot=FALSE)
res <- specprop(spec)


Please be aware that the results of timer() might not be perfect. Check them graphically.

Feedback would be welcome.

HTH,

Jerome
